html:
SMTO-BOOT-0046 — SMTO isn't allowed to open a file it needs to start

GUID: 7db587cd-ac06-470c-bac0-120090deced4
Slug: startup-permission-denied
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: startup

What happened

  • SMTO stopped while starting because your computer blocked it from reading or writing one of its files or folders.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If this screen shows Auto Fix: repair permissions and start, select it and confirm. Only the person who manages SMTO can run it. SMTO offers this only when the blocked file belongs to your own account, and it then restores your read and write access.
  2. If there's no Auto Fix button, ask the person who manages this computer to give your account access to SMTO's data folder and settings files. The blocked file may belong to another account, which only that account or an administrator can change.
  3. If SMTO was started as an administrator (for example with sudo), stop it and start it again from the account you normally use. Starting SMTO under a different account can leave files that your usual account can't open.

What success looks like

  • The startup screen reaches Ready and your conversations appear.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't fix this by always running SMTO as an administrator or by giving everyone access to its files.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Startup failed because the operating system denied the Server's account access (PermissionError) to a required file or directory, such as its configuration, data directory or TLS files.

What this means

  • The running service account lacks access to a required file or directory. The public diagnostic omits private paths; the operator should check ownership and access for the failed stage.

Why this can happen

  • The running service account lacks access to a required file or directory. The public diagnostic omits private paths; the operator should check ownership and access for the failed stage.

How to diagnose it

  • The operating system denied access to a resource needed during startup.
  • Startup reaches Ready using the intended service account.

How to fix it

  • Identify the denied path from the Server log or the Auto Fix description, then compare its owner and mode with the account that runs the Server (configuration file, AOR_AGENT_STATE_DIR, TLS certificate and key). Restore ownership to that account or grant only the read/write access it needs, then restart; do not run the Server as root to bypass it.
  • Check the service account and ownership/permissions of its configuration, runtime directory and TLS files. Grant only the required access, then restart.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded condition and run the diagnostic again. Rechecking does not replay tasks or completed operations.

How to verify the fix

  • Startup reaches Ready using the intended service account.

What not to do

  • Do not replay completed work or weaken authentication and certificate checks to clear this diagnostic.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic describes the observed failure; it does not establish the outcome of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
